title: The published fare is the last price to pay
subtitle: Four things that move a cruise fare, none of them printed on the booking page.

text: Retail is an opening position, not a price.
sub: The published fare exists so there is something to discount from. It is a starting number with a marketing calendar attached.

title: Four levers the website never shows

items.head: Contracted space held early
items.body: Blocks of cabins held at earlier rates, released through advisors rather than through a search box.

items.head: Refundable vs non-refundable
items.body: The same cabin, two prices. One of them is flexibility you may not actually need.

items.head: Credit stacked at booking
items.body: Line credit, agency credit and promotional credit are separate pots. Most travellers claim one.

items.head: Repricing after you book
items.body: Fares move. Nobody rings to tell you. A watched booking gets rebooked when it drops.

title: Where a fare is actually set

points.label: The line
points.value: Publishes a fare, then runs a promotion calendar quarter by quarter.

points.label: The agency
points.value: Holds contracted space and its own credit to apply against it.

points.label: The advisor
points.value: Decides which of those combine, on which sailing, and when.

points.label: The website
points.value: Shows you one of the three and calls it the price.

quote: Most of what I do isn't booking travel - it's editing it. The fare is part of the edit.

title: Send me a sailing you're weighing up
body: You'll get a two-line verdict: what it should cost, and whether it's the right ship for what you actually want.
